issues.line_text: What am I doing? I came here with a purpose. I can't let him distract me. Can't let myself forget why I'm here.
issues.description: Eleanor's internal monologue sounds too much like an investigator with a mission rather than a predator. 'Purpose' + 'why I'm here' reads as someone on a justice quest, not someone planning harm. Per Story Bible diagnostic questions: fails the Motive Test - she should seem to want to HURT Josh, not get ANSWERS.
issues.fix: What am I doing? I came here to end this. I can't let him distract me. Can't let myself soften now.
issues.rationale: Changes 'purpose/why I'm here' (investigator language) to 'end this' (predatory finality). 'Can't let myself soften' maintains the emotional conflict but frames it as a predator wavering in resolve, not an investigator losing objectivity.

issues.line_text: I'd left everything behindΓÇömy job, the apartment, the people who would have tried to stop me if they knew. No one understood. No one could.
issues.description: This reads as someone on a grief-driven justice mission ('no one understood' implies moral righteousness). Per Story Bible: Eleanor should read as dangerous/obsessive, not sympathetic/grieving. Fails the Stranger Test - sounds like someone seeking closure, not planning violence.
issues.fix: I'd left everything behindΓÇömy job, the apartment, the people who would have interfered if they knew what I was planning. They would have tried to stop me. They couldn't.
issues.rationale: Changes 'no one understood' (sympathy-seeking) to 'interfered/tried to stop me' (implies questionable actions). Removes emotional plea for understanding, makes her sound more calculating and isolated by choice rather than tragedy.

issues.line_text: Someone who needed to finish what she started before the opportunity slipped away.
issues.description: 'Finish what she started' + 'before opportunity slipped away' could imply terminal illness timing (she's running out of time due to cancer). Too close to revealing Reveal #2 (Eleanor is dying). Should sound more about Josh's presence being temporary, not Eleanor's time running out.
issues.fix: Someone who needed to finish this before he slipped away.
issues.rationale: Shifts focus from Eleanor's timeline to Josh's temporary presence at Thornewood. Removes 'opportunity' language that hints at Eleanor's limited time. Simpler, more predatory focus on the target.

issues.line_text: Had coffee with him today. Twenty-three minutes of small talk and careful smiles. He's charming. Too charming. The kind of man who makes you want to tell him everything.
issues.description: Journal entry reads like investigator notes documenting a subject. The time precision (twenty-three minutes) feels surveillance-oriented. Per Story Bible: Eleanor should avoid 'observation log' language in her journal.
issues.fix: Had coffee with him today. Small talk and careful smiles. He's charming. Dangerously charming. The kind of man who makes you want to trust him.
issues.rationale: Removes precise timing (feels less like surveillance logs). Changes 'tell him everything' to 'trust him' - more about emotional vulnerability than information sharing. Maintains her conflict but less investigator-coded.

issues.line_text: His questions about the trails, about the history of this placeΓÇöinnocent enough. But the way he watches everything, cataloging details, makes me uneasy. He's not just a writer on retreat. He's looking for something.
issues.description: Eleanor observing that Josh is 'cataloging details' and 'looking for something' is accurate (he IS investigating), but this makes Eleanor sound like she's tracking his investigation behavior. This is investigator-vs-investigator framing, not predator-vs-prey. Per Story Bible: she should seem to want him vulnerable, not analyzed.
issues.rationale: Reframes Josh's behavior as something that makes him seem dangerous/calculating (predator interpretation) rather than investigative (investigator interpretation). Eleanor should read his curiosity as a threat to her, not as confirmation he's investigating.

issues.line_text: I'm reading too much into nothing. The isolation is making me paranoid. Or maybe it's making me careless. I can't decide which is worse.
issues.description: This self-doubt reads more like investigator anxiety ('am I building a case on nothing?') than predator certainty. Per Story Bible: Eleanor must be CERTAIN about Josh's guilt. She shouldn't wonder if she's wrong - that implies she might be the dangerous one.
issues.fix: I'm seeing exactly what I need to see. The isolation is sharpening me. Or maybe it's making me reckless. I can't decide which is more dangerous.
issues.rationale: Flips from self-doubt to dangerous certainty. 'Seeing what I need to see' sounds obsessive (predator reading signs). 'Sharpening me' vs 'making me reckless' maintains internal conflict without questioning her core belief about Josh.

issues.line_text: I find myself wanting to trust him. That's the most dangerous thing of all. I have to remember why I came here. What happens when winter ends. What I'm going to do to him.
issues.description: Journal entry combines 'why I came here' (mission/purpose language) with 'what I'm going to do to him' (implies premeditated plan). This is too explicitly investigator/justice-seeker language. Per Story Bible: avoid mission statements. Also 'what happens when winter ends' could hint at the March confrontation timeline.
issues.fix: I find myself wanting to trust him. That's the most dangerous thing of all. I have to remember what he is. What happens when I stop pretending. What I want to do to him.
issues.rationale: 'What he is' (not why I'm here) focuses on Josh being the threat. 'When I stop pretending' implies she's holding back violence/true nature (predatory). 'Want to do to him' (not 'going to') sounds more emotional/dangerous, less calculated plan execution.

notes: Chapter 4 has significant Eleanor POV spoiler leakage. Multiple instances of investigator language ('purpose,' 'why I'm here,' 'cataloging details'), grief-driven mission framing ('no one understood'), and self-doubt about her certainty. Per Story Bible diagnostic questions, this chapter fails the Stranger Test (sounds like grieving investigator) and Motive Test (wants answers/closure, not to harm Josh). All fixes aim to maintain Eleanor's emotional conflict while reframing her internal voice as predatory/obsessive rather than investigative/sympathetic.
